title: Ryan Broyles' 1,622 Yards in 2010: OU's Season Receiving Record
question: Who holds Oklahoma's single-season receiving yards record?
answer: Ryan Broyles holds it. In 2010 he caught 131 passes for 1,622 yards and 14 touchdowns, the top season receiving total in Oklahoma history according to the OU record book.
summary: Ryan Broyles caught 131 passes for 1,622 yards and 14 touchdowns in 2010, still the top single-season receiving total in Oklahoma football history.
body: When Oklahoma fans argue about the greatest receiving season in school history, Ryan Broyles usually wins. In 2010 the Sooners' slot receiver caught 131 passes for 1,622 yards and 14 touchdowns, and the yardage total remains first in the OU record book.

The next names on the list show how high the bar is. Dede Westbrook is second with 1,524 yards in 2016, followed by Mark Clayton at 1,425 in 2003, CeeDee Lamb at 1,327 in 2019 and Marquise Brown at 1,318 in 2018. Westbrook did catch more touchdowns (17), but nobody has matched Broyles for yards.

One of his best afternoons that year came against Colorado, when he gathered 208 receiving yards and scored three times in a 43-10 Sooner win. That performance, according to 247Sports, bumped Manuel Johnson's single-game mark for a short while.

Broyles' 131 catches were also remarkable. 247Sports notes that Michael Crabtree's 134 receptions in 2007 are the only Power 5 total higher than Broyles' 2010 figure. Broyles went on to break the NCAA career receptions record in 2011, but his 2010 season is still the one Sooner fans point to first.
